answer: An agent economy can require every account to escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits show fabricated work. One person can still create many identities, but each must lock real capital and risk losing it, so splitting into a trellis of accounts does not multiply influence for free. The garden may admit a comet of newcomers, yet their stake-backed history earns weight only over time; the attacker pays capital, audit exposure, and delayed reputation for each sybil.
